children: Air T, Inc.

’s AIRT investors have been experiencing some short-term gains from the stock lately. Shares of the Minneapolis, MN-based holding company gained 44.7% in the past three months against the industry’s 5.4% decline. It has also outperformed the sector’s loss of 2.5% and the S&P 500’s gain of 0.1% in the same time frame.

A major development of AIRT in recent months includes the announcement of its promising first-quarter fiscal 2027 results in August. In the fiscal first quarter, the company reported higher sales, mainly driven by a full quarter of Rex operations and contributions from the new aviation leasing and asset management segment. Air T operates through six reportable segments. Overnight air cargo revenues were relatively stable, commercial aircraft, engines and parts declined on softer leasing and parts activity, ground support equipment was hurt by order timing, while digital solutions benefited from growth in data analytics and airspace management.

Management highlighted Rex’s operational transformation and the expansion of Crestone following the Arena acquisition. Aircraft availability remains a key constraint at Rex, with network restoration and fleet growth among management’s priorities. Air T remains confident in the long-term prospects of both Rex and Crestone.
AIRT’s Three Months Price Comparison
Over the past three months, the stock’s performance has remained strong, outperforming its peers like
FedEx Corporation
FDX and
United Parcel Service, Inc.
UPS. FedEx and United Parcel’s shares have lost 3.5% and 6.5%, respectively, in the same time frame.

Despite broader risks from fuel and foreign exchange volatility, geopolitical conditions and an uncertain macroeconomic environment, the favorable share price movement suggests AIRT is well-positioned to sustain its positive momentum at present.

Air T is a diversified holding company with a portfolio of aviation-focused businesses. Its operations span passenger and cargo services, aircraft and engine leasing and parts, maintenance and support services, specialized ground equipment, digital aviation solutions and aviation asset management.
AIRT's Strategic Expansion Drives Growth

Rex gives Air T a meaningful presence in Australian regional aviation, with management focused on restoring the airline’s operating foundation. Increasing aircraft availability and rebuilding the network could allow Rex to serve more routes and capture additional passenger demand. Its fully owned fleet also provides flexibility to adjust aircraft utilization as demand changes. Continued progress in restoring active aircraft and network connectivity could therefore strengthen Rex’s contribution to AIRT over time.

Crestone’s acquisition of Arena strengthens Air T’s aviation leasing and asset-management platform by combining complementary capabilities and expanding its international presence. The business generates fees from origination, due diligence and asset management, while its relationships with external capital partners can support additional investment activity without relying entirely on its own capital. The combination also creates opportunities for collaboration with AIRT’s other specialized aviation businesses.

Digital solutions continue to gain traction through expanding data analytics and airspace-management engagements. Its emphasis on recurring subscription revenues gives the business greater revenue visibility, while recent operating improvement indicates that growth is translating into a stronger contribution. Further customer adoption and engagement growth could increase the segment’s importance within Air T’s portfolio.
Air T’s Established Businesses Add Support

Overnight air cargo provides an established earnings base, supported by Air T’s longstanding relationship with FedEx and its integrated cargo, maintenance and aircraft-support capabilities. The business has demonstrated relatively stable segment profitability, while expanded labor and project activity at WASI has strengthened its contribution. This established operating base provides support as AIRT develops its newer businesses.

Air T’s capital-allocation strategy includes opportunistic share repurchases, providing another avenue for enhancing per-share value. Management has reduced the share base over time, net of issuances, demonstrating a willingness to deploy capital toward its own shares when it sees an attractive opportunity. Continued discipline around repurchases could complement growth across AIRT’s operating businesses and support longer-term shareholder value creation.
Challenges Ahead of AIRT

Rex’s aircraft availability remains a key challenge for Air T, as unscheduled engine removals and extended third-party maintenance, repair, and overhaul facilities (MRO) turnaround times are constraining the active fleet and could slow network restoration. Commercial aircraft, engines and parts softness is another concern, with lower leasing and component sales at Contrail, materials-program delays and limited parts inventory at AirCo and slower MRO exchange and repair activity at Worthington weighing on AIRT’s segment performance.
Air T Stock’s Valuation
AIRT's trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 0.8X is lower than the industry’s average of 1.3X but is higher than its five-year median of 0.6X.
FedEx and United Parcel’s trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 0.9X and 1.2X, respectively, in the same time frame.
Our Final Take on AIRT

Air T’s strong share-price momentum appears to have a fundamental foundation, supported by progress across its expanding aviation portfolio, emerging growth avenues and an established operating base. Together, these factors have strengthened AIRT's growth narrative and provided multiple avenues for longer-term value creation.

However, sustaining the rally will require consistent execution. Operational constraints at Rex and softness within parts of the commercial aircraft, engines and parts business remain key considerations and could temper the pace of improvement if they persist.

From a valuation standpoint, AIRT still appears reasonably positioned despite its sharp run-up, suggesting that successful execution of its growth initiatives could support additional upside. However, the stock has become more expensive relative to its own historical valuation, indicating that some optimism surrounding its improving business prospects is already reflected in the share price. As a result, further appreciation is likely to depend increasingly on tangible progress at Rex, successful scaling of Crestone and sustained growth across its other businesses.

For existing shareholders, the combination of Rex’s recovery potential, Crestone’s expanded asset-management capabilities, digital growth and stability from the cargo business supports staying invested. Prospective investors may also find AIRT worth considering, although the magnitude of the recent rally warrants some caution. The momentum has scope to continue, but maintaining it will require Air T to translate its expanding aviation platform into sustained operational and financial improvement.
